mutation_rules: Removing reservation_id, changing a relational run_id/head binding, or mutating either canonical digest must change APPROVE to HOLD.

A finding with inconclusive, not_run, or error verification must change approval to HOLD; a confirmed effective blocking finding or tier0 fail produces REJECT, while tier0 error or unavailable produces HOLD.
Changing only provider/model attribution, with its canonical evidence and reservation digests recomputed, must not change the outcome.
The run_id date, timestamp UTC date, exact task map, finding identity, and task/tier binding are immutable acceptance inputs.
digest_algorithm: sha256(name NUL bytes NUL, in files order; corpus excludes digests.json)
non_coverage: Synthetic records prove structure, relations, and digest behavior only; they do not prove external provider or accounting authenticity. A later production adapter must obtain authoritative provider and accounting evidence and fail closed when it cannot. Provider changes alone are neutral. Initial Oracle adoption relies on Guard+Owner-Audit+adversarial review; after merge, a separate freeze/activation Guard-PR v2 must make the corpus immutable before candidate derivation.
